lead_headline: Lost Coffee debuts sixth Colorado location in Arvada today, capping a weekend that saw 9 new restaurant leads including FiNO's Mediterranean opening at the All Inn Hotel and multiple closures across Cherry Creek and Westminster

restaurant.blurb: 9 new leads since Friday: FiNO (City Park), Lost Coffee (Arvada), Ash and Agave (Cherry Creek), Paperboy Denver (Highlands), Dumplin' closure (Highlands), Mojo-99 Burgers closure (Westminster). Active: 140 total.

liquor.blurb: Zero applications today extends the post-flood silence to four consecutive days, keeping the 7-day total frozen at 2,144 licenses — still running 764% above last week's 248 filings — as the backend processing surge that peaked mid-week continues its slow decay. The anomaly now represents 99.4% of this week's volume, with the rolling window set to begin shedding the spike as April's batch renewals exit the count. Historical baselines of 20-30 weekly filings should return by mid-May once the mass-filing event fully clears the seven-day window.

reputation.blurb: Zero mentions yesterday drops the 7-day count to 43 across 13 sources — down 16% from last week's 51 mentions — as Sunday's complete editorial blackout confirms the weekend slowdown that began Saturday. The 43-mention pace still tracks 5% above April's 41-weekly average, but three consecutive days of minimal activity (1 mention Friday, 1 Saturday, 0 Sunday) marks May's sharpest deceleration yet. Instagram maintains its grip with 16 pickups (37% of weekly volume), followed by Denver Post (6), Facebook (5), X (4), and Reddit (3). Monday typically brings a news cycle reset, but the sustained weekend silence suggests traditional outlets remain in post-April coast mode while social channels provide baseline coverage.

subscriptions.blurb: Net +5 since Friday (6 new, 1 canceled) lifts MTD to +5 (+1.7/day), with 90-day net holding at +123. The weekend's steady gains — zero activity Saturday, +2 Friday, +3 Thursday — temporarily mask the underlying churn crisis: this week's −2 net (18 new, 20 canceled) marks a sharp reversal from last week's +17 and exposes persistent cancellation pressure that's now neutralizing new subscriber momentum. MTD's +1.7/day rate runs 31% above YTD's +1.3/day baseline, but the April 28th mass-cancellation event (17 losses in one day) continues rippling through the data. Until daily churn returns to single digits and conversion stabilizes, May's opening gains remain fragile despite Friday-Sunday's brief respite.
